summary: IcebergConnectionBase — abstract base for all Iceberg catalog connections. Provides full lifecycle (connect/disconnect/reconnect), schema caching, table loading with retry, inspection (list_namespaces, list_tables, inspect_table, inspect_namespace, inspect_catalog), existence checks, DataFrame accessors (to_ibis, to_polars), and mutation delegation wrappers to operations.py.
extension_points: catalog_backend abstract property — return the live pyiceberg Catalog handle
lifecycle_notes: Inherits from legacy BaseDBConnection — settings-driven construction via SettingsParameters.
Schema cache (_schema_cache) is in-memory and per-instance — cleared on disconnect.
table() has built-in retry logic (max_attempts=3, retry_delay=0.5s) for transient catalog errors.
Mutations delegate to operations.py via local imports to avoid circular deps.
to_relation() is explicitly NOT implemented — waiting on mountainash-expressions Iceberg adapter.
documentation_hooks: Schema cache behaviour and when to call clear_schema_cache() deserves documentation
DataFrame accessor methods (table_as_ibis_dataframe, table_as_polars_dataframe) are a user-facing feature
risks: connect_default() hardcodes self._catalog_backend = RestCatalog(**kwargs) regardless of subclass — may not work for non-REST catalogs
table_exists/view_exists return None (not False) when not connected — implicit falsy but type-incorrect
open_questions: Should IcebergConnectionBase drop BaseDBConnection inheritance and use a cleaner settings-injection pattern?

evidence.detail: 500+ line class with full Iceberg lifecycle and DataFrame accessors
